🏦 Thinking of a two-pot withdrawal for December? Know what it really costs first.

The rules:
🔹 You can withdraw from your savings pot once per tax year (March to February), at least R2,000.
🔹 The money is added to your income and taxed at your marginal rate. A big withdrawal can push you into a higher bracket.
🔹 If you owe SARS, it can take that tax debt from the payout first.
🔹 The tax directive and fund processing can take weeks, so the money may not arrive before Christmas. You must be registered for tax, and fees may apply.

Example (illustrative): you withdraw R20,000 and your marginal rate is 26% (roughly R245,000 to R383,000 taxable income a year). About R5,200 goes to tax, so you get about R14,800 before fees.

It's money taken from your retirement, plus the growth it would have earned. Please don't raid your retirement for Black Friday.

General information, not financial advice.
